subject: Game Theory
title: Gender and Negotiation
description: A micro-lesson that makes Gender and Negotiation usable.

hook.text: Studies show men negotiate starting salaries four times more often than women do.

buildup.text: The gap isn't about skill. Women who negotiate assertively face social backlash that men don't experience.

discovery.text: Researchers call this the 'social cost of negotiation'—women are penalized for behavior rewarded in men.

twist.text: When women negotiate on behalf of others, the backlash disappears. The penalty targets self-advocacy specifically.

climax.text: Organizations that standardize compensation and use transparent pay bands reduce the gender gap significantly.

punchline.text: Systems shape fairness more than individuals.

quiz.question: Why do women negotiate less often?
options: They face social penalties for assertive self-advocacy
